title: Neutron multiplier material scarcity for blankets
bottleneck: Many breeding blanket designs rely on beryllium as a neutron multiplier to achieve tritium breeding ratios above 1.0, but beryllium is toxic, expensive, and produced in tiny quantities, with global production of a few hundred tonnes per year from a single dominant supplier. A fleet of fusion plants would need thousands of tonnes, and irradiated beryllium swells, cracks, and generates tritium and helium that complicate recycling.
why_it_blocks: A blanket concept that depends on a material the world cannot supply at fleet scale is a dead end. Multiplier availability constrains blanket design as tightly as physics does.
current_state: Alternative multipliers like lead are used in lithium-lead blankets to sidestep beryllium. Beryllium-based pebble-bed blankets face unresolved supply and lifetime questions.
